instructions:
WARNING: You MUST follow the steps below or EVERY tool call will fail.

You are connected to a godot-mcp server that gates its tools into categories called 'toolsets'. Only 'core' (diagnostics, toolset management) and 'inspection' (read-only project/scene/node reading) are enabled by default. Every other capability is hidden until you explicitly enable it.

MANDATORY PROTOCOL — follow this order exactly:
1. Call godot_get_server_info() for a full capability snapshot (toolsets, bridge state, troubleshooting).
2. Call godot_list_toolsets() to see what is available and which are enabled — this is the authoritative enabled state, not any static claim in this text.
3. Call godot_enable_toolset(category) for every category you plan to use that godot_list_toolsets() reports as disabled. It also accepts a comma-separated list of toolsets or a bundle — author / playtest / ship — so a whole workflow is one call.
4. Only after a toolset is enabled can you call the tools in it.

WARNING: calling a gated tool whose toolset is disabled fails with "Tool '<name>' is not enabled". There is NO fallback.

QUICK DECISION TREE — what do you want to do?
- Build/edit scenes, add/move/remove nodes, change properties → scene_edit
- Write/attach GDScript, fix parse errors → scripts
- Run the game live in the editor (play, inspect, simulate input) → runtime + input
- Pause/step/inspect stack at a line → debugger + runtime
- Assert a node property meets an expectation → testing + runtime
- Apply changes to many nodes at once → batch + scene_edit
- Physics bodies, collision shapes, gravity/materials → physics + scene_edit
- Register autoloads, create custom resources → resources_edit
- Performance, bottlenecks → profiling
- Circular deps, unused resources, signal flow → analysis
- Export a build for a platform → export
- Import textures/audio/models → asset_import

Common toolsets you will need:
- scene_edit  → godot_scene_edit_create_node, godot_scene_edit_set_node_property, godot_scene_edit_attach_script, godot_scene_edit_save_scene
- scripts     → godot_scripts_write, godot_scripts_read, godot_scripts_get_parse_errors
- runtime     → godot_runtime_run_and_capture (headless), godot_runtime_play_scene (editor)
- input       → godot_input_simulate_action, godot_input_simulate_key, godot_input_play_sequence
- testing     → godot_testing_assert_node_state, godot_testing_run_test_scenario
- batch       → godot_batch_set_property, godot_batch_find_nodes_by_type
- physics     → godot_physics_setup_body, godot_physics_setup_collision
- resources_edit → godot_resources_edit_register_autoload, godot_resources_edit_create_resource
- asset_import → godot_asset_import_asset, godot_asset_import_create_material_from_textures

SERVER VS ADDON BOUNDARY:
Some tools run in the Python server (godot_list_toolsets, godot_enable_toolset, godot_get_server_info) and never message Godot. Most tools send commands to the Godot addon via a WebSocket bridge. "Tool '<name>' is not enabled" means the toolset is not enabled OR you confused a server-side tool with an addon tool — call godot_enable_toolset first.

SAFETY CONVENTION (every mutating tool):
- Mutating tools accept dry_run=True — they report what WOULD change and perform nothing. Preview first when unsure.
- Destructive tools (delete/overwrite, e.g. godot_scene_edit_delete_node, godot_scene_edit_reload_scene) require confirm=True or they refuse to run; they also support dry_run.
- Read-only tools never mutate and need neither flag.

DOCUMENTATION:
- Tutorial: https://github.com/hybridindie/godot-mcp/blob/main/TUTORIAL.md
- Tool contracts: https://github.com/hybridindie/godot-mcp/blob/main/docs/tool-contracts.md
- Architecture: https://github.com/hybridindie/godot-mcp/blob/main/docs/architecture.md

This server also exposes workflow prompts (toolset_discovery, build_scene, play_test, script_edit, debug_scene, troubleshoot) and a diagnostics tool (godot_get_server_info) that returns tool counts, bridge state, active scene, and common errors with fixes.
